title: Bus FX & Printing Effects
blurb: Shape a pad with MFX, drive the whole beat through Bus FX, then resample to commit the sound.

steps.title: Per-pad MFX versus the bus
body: MFX applies to a single pad, so use it to fix or characterise one sound — a filter on a bassline, saturation on a snare.
BUS FX applies to everything running through it, so use it to glue the whole beat together.
Knowing which one you want saves you from processing a sound twice by mistake.
steps.checkpoint: You can state, out loud, which of the two you need for the change you have in mind.
steps.tip: If you want the effect on a single element, reach for MFX. If you want it on the beat, reach for Bus FX.

steps.title: Put MFX on one pad
body: Select the pad you want to process, then assign an MFX type to it.
Use the CTRL knobs to adjust the effect's parameters while the pad plays.
Keep it musical: a small amount of filtering or saturation usually does more than an extreme setting.
steps.checkpoint: That one pad sounds different; every other pad is untouched.
steps.tip: Adjust with the pad looping so you hear the change in context rather than in isolation.

steps.title: Run the beat through Bus FX
body: Press BUS FX and choose an effect for the whole mix.
The vinyl-style and filter effects are what give this unit much of its signature character — try them first.
Tweak with the CTRL knobs while your beat loops, and stop when it sounds better, not when you have explored everything.
steps.checkpoint: The entire beat is coloured by the effect, and it feels like one cohesive sound.
steps.tip: Bus FX is a performance tool too — sweeping a filter live over a loop is an instant arrangement change.

steps.title: Print the effect with a resample
body: Effects are live until you commit them. To make the processed sound permanent, resample it to a new pad.
Press RESAMPLE, pick an empty pad, hit REC to arm, then play the beat through the effect.
Stop recording at the end of your loop. The new pad now contains the effected audio.
Because the effect is baked in, your Bus FX slot is free to process the new pad again.
steps.checkpoint: The new pad sounds effected even with Bus FX switched off.
steps.tip: This stacking trick — print, then process again — is how you build heavily textured, layered sounds on a unit with one bus.

steps.title: Know when to stop
body: Every resample pass is committed and cannot be undone, so keep the clean version on its original pad until you are certain.
Two or three considered passes beat ten reactive ones.
When the beat sounds finished, stop processing and start arranging it instead.
steps.tip: Back up to an SD card before a heavy printing session. It is the only real undo you have.
